note: The main banks, chosen as the best-known large card issuers (no central bank ranking was read): Kaspi Bank, Halyk Bank and Bank CenterCredit. Kaspi's credit card page didn't answer this research's connections on 2026-10-30 (nor did Jusan's), and wasn't read. Bank CenterCredit: its #картакарта credit card is free to issue and hold, and charges 26.99% a year outside its grace period (24.99% for clients paid through the bank's salary projects, who aren't modeled). Halyk Bank's three credit card pages, read on 2026-10-30 (its tariffs page links only a tariff for cards issued before 27 July 2018, which isn't written): My!Card and DARA cost nothing to hold and bear 30% a year; Infinite Credit costs 72,000 tenge a year, charged at issue for the first year and nothing in later years when the card's turnover in the previous year is over 5 million tenge (written as a waiver on that spending), and bears 25% a year. Each card's minimum payment is 1% of the debt and at least 2,000 tenge. Their interest-free periods run up to 45 days (My!Card, on purchases, transfers and cash) and up to 60 days (Infinite Credit, on all three; DARA, on purchases only); the transfer and cash withdrawal fee is 4% on My!Card and 2% on DARA, and a cash withdrawal costs 3% on Infinite Credit (transfers 2%, not written). Wave 4 (2026-10-30): no bank was added. Tried: Freedom Bank's cards page offers no credit card (its cards carry cashback and an investment account); Kaspi, Home Credit and Eurasian Bank didn't answer; ForteBank's address answered not found; Bereke Bank's home page linked no credit card; a search for these banks' credit card tariffs found none. Wave 5 (2026-10-30), minimum payments: No minimum payment is published for Bank CenterCredit's #картакарта; tried: its card page and its tariffs of 29 January 2026 (read 2026-10-30, no minimum), a Russian web search (only the bank's different #180 card, 5% of the principal, in the press), and archive.org (no answer).
